// Resources/Dialogue/sheriff_intro.txt
//
// The first meeting. Sets `met_sheriff`, which a rematch file can read.
//
// Doubles as the format's worked example. A two-hander on purpose: SHERIFF holds the right side and
// {PLAYER} the left, so both portraits are exercised and the dimming reads. Every piece of the
// grammar appears at least once — TMP colour, all four motion effects, both timing cues, a tag gate,
// a negated gate, a timer with a fallback, fallthrough, and an explicit END.
//
// Note this file names SHERIFF rather than using {ENEMY}. That is the choice between a scene written
// for one specific opponent and one reusable across several — see the catalogue notes. Don't use
// both for the same character: they are two speakers as far as the portrait staging is concerned,
// and they would fight over the same side.

# opening
SHERIFF: You picked the <color=#c81e1e>wrong town</color>, stranger.
{PLAYER}: I've heard that one before.
SHERIFF: Ten paces.[pause=0.4] [shake]You know how this goes.[/shake]

# threat
@timer 4 -> back_down
SHERIFF: Well?[pause=0.5] Say something.
> "Just passing through."                 -> passing
> "You talk a lot for a dead man."        -> insult
> [met_sheriff] "We've met before."       -> callback
> [!cocky] Say nothing.                   -> back_down

# insult
@tag cocky
@perk Scattershot
{PLAYER}: You talk a lot for a dead man.
SHERIFF: [wobble=1.4]...Ten paces. Now.[/wobble]
-> END

# passing
@tag polite
@tag met_sheriff
{PLAYER}: Just passing through.
SHERIFF: Nobody's just passing. Not here.
SHERIFF: [speed=0.6]Not any more.[/speed]
-> END

# callback
@tag met_sheriff
{PLAYER}: We've met before.
SHERIFF: [wave]So we have.[/wave] Didn't finish it then either.
-> END

# back_down
@tag met_sheriff
SHERIFF: [jump]Thought so.[/jump]
// No jump: the last node simply ends the conversation.
